title: Face projections and prime quotients of complete monoid models
statement:
Let $P$ be a finitely generated integral saturated additive commutative monoid [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], with $0$ its only invertible element, and let $n\ge0$. Let $S\subseteq P$ be an additive submonoid which is a face, meaning that $a+b\in S$ with $a,b\in P$ implies $a,b\in S$. For a local ring $L$ with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_L$, put
$$B_L(P,n)=\varprojlim_N L[P][t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(\mathfrak m_L,z^q\ (q\ne0),t_1,\ldots,t_n)^N,$$
and define $B_L(S,n)$ in the same way [def-trf-complete-toric-model, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let $L$ be either a field $k$, or a Cohen ring $C$ of residue characteristic a prime $p$ [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring]. Then $S$ is also finitely generated, integral, saturated and sharp; if $g_1,\ldots,g_s$ generate $P$, their subset in $S$ generates $S$. There is a surjective $L$-algebra map $\rho:B_L(P,n)\to B_L(S,n)$ which, under the coefficient-family descriptions, retains exactly the coefficients at exponents $(q,e)\in S\times\mathbf N^n$. Its kernel is
$$J_S=(z^{g_i}:g_i\notin S)B_L(P,n)=(z^q:q\notin S)B_L(P,n).$$
For $R=B_k(P,n)$ put $\mathfrak p_S=J_S$. For $R=B_C(P,n)/(\theta)$ with $\theta-p\in(z^q\ (q\ne0),t_1,\ldots,t_n)B_C(P,n)$, let $\mathfrak p_S$ be the image of $J_S$ and put $\theta_S=\rho(\theta)$. In the second case $\theta_S-p\in(z^s\ (s\in S\setminus\{0\}),t_1,\ldots,t_n)B_C(S,n)$. There are isomorphisms preserving constants and the surviving chart monomials
$$R/\mathfrak p_S\cong B_k(S,n)\quad\hbox{or}\quad R/\mathfrak p_S\cong B_C(S,n)/(\theta_S),$$
respectively. Each displayed quotient is a nonzero normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], $\mathfrak p_S$ is prime, and $z^q\in\mathfrak p_S$ if and only if $q\notin S$. The cases $S=P$, $S=\{0\}$ and $n=0$ are included.

proof.text: First check the hypotheses for the face monoid. If $s\in S$ is expressed as a sum of the generators $g_i$ of $P$, repeated application of the face condition shows that every summand belongs to $S$. Thus the subset of generators in $S$ generates $S$. Integrality and sharpness are inherited from $P$. For saturation identify $S^{\rm gp}$ with the subgroup it generates in $P^{\rm gp}$, using integrality. If $x\in S^{\rm gp}$ and $a x\in S$ for an integer $a>0$, saturation of $P$ first gives $x\in P$; the face condition applied to the sum of $a$ copies of $x$ then gives $x\in S$. This proves that $S$ is fine, saturated and sharp, using precisely the definitions in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup].

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70, supplies the model notation only; Q46 agent coefficient argument for face quotients.

proof.text: Use [lem-trf-sharp-fs-orthant-embedding] to embed $P$ in $\mathbf N^r\subset\mathbf Z^r$ by $\lambda$. In $H=\mathbf Z^{r+n}$ put $T_P=\lambda(P)\times\mathbf N^n$ and $T_S=\lambda(S)\times\mathbf N^n$. Both are finitely generated, and the sum $W$ of the coordinates of $H$ is strictly positive on each monoid away from zero. Renaming $z^q t^e$ as $z^{(\lambda(q),e)}$ identifies $L[P][t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ with $L[T_P]$, and likewise for $S$; nonzero pairs generate exactly the chart ideals, so these renamings induce inverse maps on every quotient defining the completions. A field is a PID, and a Cohen ring is a complete local PID with nonzero uniformizer $p$ by [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring]. Hence both coefficient rings are Noetherian domains by [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal], complete and separated for their maximal ideals (for a field the ideal is zero). Apply [lem-trf-complete-model-coefficient-nonvanishing] to $T_P,T_S$. It identifies the two completions with all coefficient families indexed by $P\times\mathbf N^n$ and $S\times\mathbf N^n$, respectively, with finite convolution multiplication and the stipulated chart monomials.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70, supplies the model notation only; Q46 agent coefficient argument for face quotients.

proof.text: Define $\rho$ by restriction of these families to $S\times\mathbf N^n$. For $s\in S$, every decomposition $s=a+b$ in $P$ has $a,b\in S$, so the finite convolution coefficient of a product at $(s,e)$ is unchanged by restriction. Restriction also preserves addition, $1$, and constants; hence it is an $L$-algebra map. Extending any family by zero outside $S\times\mathbf N^n$ gives a preimage, proving surjectivity. Its kernel consists exactly of the families supported at pairs $(q,e)$ with $q\notin S$.

proof.text: In the field case the map $[b]\mapsto\rho(b)$ identifies $B_k(P,n)/J_S$ with $B_k(S,n)$: it is onto and two representatives have the same image exactly when their difference is in the kernel from Step 4. In the Cohen case the composite map $b\mapsto[\rho(b)]$ onto $B_C(S,n)/(\theta_S)$ has kernel $J_S+(\theta)$. Indeed, if $\rho(b)=\theta_S c$, choose a lift $\widetilde c$ under $\rho$; then $b-\theta\widetilde c\in J_S$, and the converse is immediate. Factoring first by $(\theta)$ therefore gives exactly $R/\mathfrak p_S$ and the asserted isomorphism. Every map fixes constants and surviving monomials. Applying $\rho$ to the hypothesis on $\theta-p$ gives $\theta_S-p$ in the displayed chart ideal: each generator maps either to zero, a surviving $z^s$ with $s\ne0$, or the same variable $t_i$.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70, supplies the model notation only; Q46 agent coefficient argument for face quotients.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-log-regular-saturation-normality] with monoid $S$, which satisfies all its finiteness, integrality, saturation and sharpness hypotheses by Step 1. In the Cohen case Step 5 supplies exactly its hypothesis $\theta_S-p$ in the chart ideal, with the original Cohen ring and prime $p$; in the field case use the original field $k$. Thus both quotient rings of Step 5 are nonzero normal domains. Their kernels $\mathfrak p_S$ in $R$ are prime: $1$ has nonzero image, and a product has zero image only if one factor has zero image in the domain.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70, supplies the model notation only; Q46 agent coefficient argument for face quotients.

proof.text: For $q\notin S$, the chart monomial maps to zero under $\rho$, hence belongs to $\mathfrak p_S$. If $q\in S$, its image is $z^q$ in the corresponding model for $S$. In the field case this family has coefficient $1$ at $(q,0)$, so is nonzero. In the Cohen case, the coefficient at $(0,0)$ of $\theta_S$ is exactly $p$: every generator of the chart ideal has zero constant coefficient by finite convolution and sharpness. We have $p\in\mathfrak m_C\setminus\{0\}$ by [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring], so [lem-trf-complete-model-coefficient-nonvanishing], with $A=C$, $T=T_S$ and $r=p$, says that every $z^{(\lambda(q),0)}$ survives modulo $(\theta_S)$. Thus $z^q\notin\mathfrak p_S$. For $S=P$ the complementary generator list is empty and $\rho$ is the identity; for $S=\{0\}$ it retains exactly $q=0$, leaving the power-series variables. The same formulas work for $n=0$ and $P=\{0\}$, where $W$ may be zero on the ambient zero group because there is no nonzero monoid element to test.
